'''''Gladiolus palustris''''', common name '''marsh gladiolus''' or '''sword lily''', is a [[herbaceous]] [[perennial]] plant belonging to the genus ''[[Gladiolus]]'' of the family [[Iridaceae]]. The genus name ''Gladiolus'' is the Latin diminutive of gladius, a sword, while the specific Latin name ''palustris'', meaning ''growing in marshes'', refers to the alleged environment of this species.

==Description==
''Gladiolus palustris'' reaches on average {{convert|30|-|60|cm}} of height. The stem is erect, glabrous and unbranched, the bulbus is spherical with cross-linked fibers at the top. The leaves are shorter than the stem, simple, with a parallel venation, sword-shaped, {{convert|4|-|9|cm}} long.  The inflorescence is composed of three to six hermaphroditic flowers, trifoliate, with a rosy violet or magenta perigonium, about {{convert|30|cm}} long. The flowering period of these plants extends from May through July. They are pollinated by bumblebees.

==Distribution==
This species is native of Central and NW Europe. It occurs in eastern [[France]], [[Switzerland]],  in southern and eastern [[Germany]], the [[Czech Republic]], [[Slovakia]] and [[Poland]]. It is present in the Italian Alps, [[Austria]] and [[Hungary]] and more common in the Balkan region. Other locations are in Eastern Europe, including [[Romania]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Miu |first1=Iulia V. |last2=Rozylowicz |first2=Laurentiu |last3=Popescu |first3=Viorel D. |last4=Anastasiu |first4=Paulina |title=Identification of areas of very high biodiversity value to achieve the EU Biodiversity Strategy for 2030 key commitments |journal=PeerJ |date=2020 |volume=8 |article-number=e10067 |doi=10.7717/peerj.10067|pmid=33062449 |pmc=7532765 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Habitat==
Notwithstanding the name, these plants do not grow in marshes, as they prefer calcareous, moist and humus rich environments alternately wet and dry, in [[wet meadow]]s and forest clearings.  They can be found at a maximum altitude of {{convert|1200|-|1500|m}}.
